sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 CLDF sources.bib (house copy), all entries coded for Bile [bil] or mentioning Jarawan/Bille.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Bile-coded entries: Maddieson & Williamson 1975 (overview;comparative;wordlist), Blench 2006 (overview;comparative;wordlist), Thomas 1927 (overview;wordlist), Gerhardt 1982 and 1988, Lukas & Gerhardt 1981 (Mbula, miscoded to Bile), Green & Grollemund 2022 (conference paper, 28 pp.), Rueck, Yoder & Hannelova 2007 (sociolinguistic survey ms., Jos). No grammar, grammar sketch, phonology or dictionary of Bile exists in Glottolog.

sources.citation: Green, Christopher R. 2020. Harmony and disharmony in Mbat (Jarawan Bantu) verbs. Linguistique et Langues Africaines 6: 43-72. DOI 10.4000/lla.289.
sources.access_detail: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: About Mbat (Bankal), not Bile: 'three main surface tone levels — High, Mid, and Low'; says of the c. 20 Jarawan languages that prior work was mostly lexical. No mention of Bile or of stress (per the openedition page summary).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2011. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, 3rd edition (version May 2011). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 64 'Ɓile', p. 14.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Catalogue entry only: names (Bille, Bili, Bilanci; Kun-Ɓíilé; ɓa Ɓíilé), location (Numan LGA, 25 km S of Numan), 30,000 speakers (CAPRO 1992), 'Jarawan Bantu', 'said to be intercomprehensible with Mbula'. Sources listed: Blench (1990); Kleinewillinghöfer (1992); Rueck et al. (2009); Refs: Maddieson & Williamson (1975); CAPRO (1992). No phonological source named.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2006. Jarawan Bantu: new data and its relation to Bantu. Working document, Cambridge, 12 January 2006, 20 pp. (Bile column from Ulrich Kleinewillinghöfer's unpublished SFB 268 wordlist, early 1990s).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Comparative wordlist (pp. 3-15) with a tone-marked Bile column (e.g. ash túbú, belly bú`m); no phonological description, no mention of stress or accent anywhere in the document.

sources.citation: Gerhardt, Ludwig. 1988. A note on verbal extensions in Jarawan Bantu. Journal of West African Languages 18(2): 3-8.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The paper treats verbal extensions in Jaar (Jarawa) and Kantana (Mama) only; Bile is not mentioned at all (only listed via Maddieson & Williamson's classification as 'Numan group'). No word on stress, accent or tone. The scanned string 'Heavy stress' on p. 6 is a misread of 'Heavy stems' (Table 3).

sources.citation: Thomas, Northcote W. 1927. The Bantu languages of Nigeria. In Festschrift Meinhof, 65-72. Hamburg: L. Friederichsen.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Short comparative wordlist in which 'Bi.' = Bili (e.g. blood nkila Bar. Bi. Mbu; tooth mila Bi.) plus a location table (Bili, Br., 11°55'/9°15'); no prosodic remarks.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page bile1244; Wikipedia 'Bile language' and 'Jarawan languages' pages.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Glottolog lists only Gerhardt 1988 as descriptive literature and Maddieson & Williamson 1975 / Green & Grollemund 2022 for subclassification; Wikipedia gives the autonym Kun-Ɓíilé and cites Ethnologue and Blench 2019 Atlas, plus Blench 2026 Jos Linguistic Circle talk on Jarawan (academia.edu, not fetchable).
